question: Should the heartbeat status mismatch be solved by renaming the row to `Heartbeat config`, or should this PR wait for scheduler/default alignment or a durable observed-telemetry surface instead?
rationale: The patch intentionally clarifies that the row is config-derived rather than making the displayed cadence match observed delivery, and the row-label rename has compatibility impact for human-readable status scraping.

options.title: Accept label clarification after proof
options.body: Keep the narrow row-label/docs/test fix, require live CLI proof and changelog removal, and accept the text-output compatibility risk as intentional.

options.title: Require cadence alignment
options.body: Reject the label-only fix and instead require status, scheduler defaults, and observed-delivery telemetry to converge before closing the issue.

options.title: Close stale branch later
options.body: If contributor proof and conflict cleanup do not arrive after the cleanup threshold, close this PR and keep the canonical issue for a replacement fix.

recommendation.title: Accept label clarification after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the narrow row-label/docs/test fix, require live CLI proof and changelog removal, and accept the text-output compatibility risk as intentional.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the status CLI presentation surface where this person has the strongest recent history signal.
